$comment: Source of truth for team MCP servers. tools/mcp.mjs reads it to write configs and the README table. Every server here was checked free on 2026-10-28. Tokens are always ${VAR} references, never values.

groups.database: Per project, read-only, never production (see database-safety.md)
groups.platform: Per project, for whoever deploys or works on payments
groups.security: Pilot first; sends code to a vendor unless noted
groups.research: Personal, on your own free account and credits

servers.name: NextSprint
servers.use: Read and update your cards: move, checklist, comments, PR link
servers.free: Internal NextPak board
servers.safety: Delete tools are blocked; deletions are done by a person in the board UI.

servers.name: Playwright
servers.use: Drive a real browser: user journeys, forms, screenshots, console errors
servers.free: Yes, open source, no account
servers.safety: Not a security boundary. Use test accounts only, never real customer logins.

servers.name: Context7
servers.use: Current docs and examples for any library before writing code against it
servers.free: Yes. Works without a key (rate limited); a free key from context7.com/dashboard raises limits
servers.safety: Read-only by nature. Your questions are sent to Context7; don't paste secrets into them.

servers.name: GitHub
servers.use: Read PRs, issues, Actions logs and code across repos (read-only)
servers.free: Yes, all GitHub plans; Copilot-only tools excluded
servers.auth: Fine-grained personal access token in GITHUB_PAT (read access to the repos you work on)
servers.safety: Read-only and limited toolsets. Pushing and opening PRs stay with git and the gh CLI (pr-ready).

servers.name: Sentry
servers.use: Production errors: stack traces, events, affected releases for a Sentry issue link
servers.free: Yes, any Sentry plan. Seer (AI root cause) is paid; the rest works without it
servers.auth: Sign in when prompted (OAuth, your Sentry role)
servers.safety: Error events can contain user data; summarize, never paste raw events into cards or PRs.

servers.name: Chrome DevTools
servers.use: Debug a page: network requests, console with source maps, performance traces, Lighthouse
servers.free: Yes, open source, no account
servers.safety: Isolated profile, usage statistics off. Use test accounts only.

servers.name: Next.js DevTools
servers.use: Live build, runtime and type errors, routes and logs from a running Next.js 16+ dev server
servers.free: Yes, open source, no account
servers.safety: Local dev server only.

servers.name: shadcn/ui
servers.use: Search and add components from the shadcn registries in components.json
servers.free: Yes, public registry needs no account
servers.safety: Only projects that already use shadcn/ui.

servers.name: DBHub (Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server)
servers.use: Inspect schema and run read-only SQL on a dev or staging database
servers.free: Yes, open source, no account
servers.safety: readonly = true and max_rows in dbhub.toml, plus a read-only database user. Never production.

servers.name: MongoDB
servers.use: Inspect collections and run read-only queries on a dev or staging MongoDB
servers.free: Yes for self-managed and Atlas databases (Atlas admin tools need extra credentials; not used)
servers.auth: Connection string of a read-only user in MDB_MCP_CONNECTION_STRING
servers.safety: --readOnly removes write tools; the database user must have only the read role. Never production.

servers.name: Supabase
servers.use: Inspect tables, run read-only SQL, read logs and docs for one dev or staging project
servers.free: Yes, free Supabase account (branching tools are paid; not used)
servers.auth: Sign in when prompted (OAuth). Project ref in SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF
servers.safety: read_only=true and one project only. SUPABASE_PROJECT_REF must be a dev or staging project, never production.

servers.name: Firebase
servers.use: Read Firestore documents and Auth users in a dev Firebase project
servers.free: Yes, part of the Firebase CLI
servers.auth: Your Firebase CLI login (firebase login); select the dev project with firebase use
servers.safety: No read-only mode: write tools are blocked here. Dev Firebase project only, never one with real users.

servers.name: Vercel
servers.use: Deployment status, build logs, runtime errors and logs for your projects
servers.free: Yes, all plans including Hobby
servers.auth: Sign in when prompted (OAuth, your Vercel role)
servers.safety: No read-only mode and ~200 tools: deploys, env vars, domains, DNS, firewall and purchases are blocked. Not for Antigravity (over its 100-tool limit and not an approved Vercel client).

servers.name: Stripe
servers.use: Look up test customers, payments, subscriptions and docs while building payment features
servers.free: Yes, free Stripe account and sandboxes
servers.auth: Sign in when prompted (OAuth). Authorize sandboxes only, never live mode
servers.safety: Sandbox only; write tools blocked. From 2026-11-30 Stripe rejects plain secret keys for MCP, so use OAuth.

servers.name: DeepWiki
servers.use: Ask questions about any public GitHub repo (a library's internals, how a project works)
servers.free: Yes, no account for public repos
servers.safety: Public repos only. Never ask it about private code.

servers.name: Serena
servers.use: Symbol-level navigation and refactoring in large codebases (find references, rename)
servers.free: Yes, open source, runs locally
servers.requires: uv tool install -p 3.13 serena-agent (adds the serena command)
servers.safety: Fully local. Little benefit on small projects.

servers.name: Semgrep
servers.use: Scan changed code for security issues before a PR
servers.free: Yes, Semgrep CLI scans locally for free (Semgrep Secrets is paid; not used)
servers.requires: pip install semgrep (or brew install semgrep)
servers.safety: Local scanning; code stays on your machine.

servers.name: Snyk
servers.use: Scan dependencies and code for known vulnerabilities
servers.free: Yes, free Snyk account; about 100 code tests per month, so scan on demand
servers.auth: Log in through the snyk_auth tool the first time
servers.safety: Code scans run in Snyk's cloud: only on repos the client allows to leave the machine.

servers.name: GitGuardian
servers.use: Find hardcoded secrets in the code you're about to push
servers.free: Yes, free Starter plan up to 25 developers
servers.safety: Scanned content is sent to GitGuardian. Some tools change incidents; review before approving.

servers.name: Exa
servers.use: Web search and page fetch for research
servers.free: Yes, works without a key; free account adds monthly credit
servers.safety: Queries go to Exa; no code or secrets in them.

servers.name: Tavily
servers.use: Web search and page extraction for research
servers.free: Yes, 1,000 credits/month on the free plan
servers.safety: Queries go to Tavily; no code or secrets in them.

servers.name: Firecrawl
servers.use: Scrape or crawl a site into clean text (docs sites, competitor pages)
servers.free: Yes, 1,000 credits/month on the free plan
servers.safety: Only public pages; respect site terms.

servers.name: Bright Data
servers.use: Search and scrape pages that block simple fetches
servers.free: Yes, 5,000 requests/month on the free tier
servers.safety: Only public pages; respect site terms.

servers.name: SerpApi
servers.use: Google search results (rankings, SERP features)
servers.free: Yes, but only 250 searches/month: personal use
servers.safety: Queries go to SerpApi.

excluded.name: Figma Dev Mode
excluded.reason: Needs a paid Figma plan; the team rarely uses Figma

excluded.name: Postman
excluded.reason: Free plan is one user; add per person if a project uses Postman collections

excluded.name: Sequential Thinking
excluded.reason: Current models already reason step by step; adds tokens without a clear gain

excluded.name: Memory / knowledge-graph servers
excluded.reason: Decisions belong in the repo as ADRs (docs-keeper), not in agent memory

excluded.name: Filesystem, Git, Fetch servers
excluded.reason: Agents already have these as built-in tools
